correctness.rationale: The source z-formula specializes to z_J=binom(a+c+1,2)+b with k=a+b+c. Writing t=a+c gives z_J=k+t(t-1)/2<=binom(k+1,2). At the uniform center, this yields subset-hyperplane slack at least k(N-k)/2. Projection of a k-subset indicator to the trace-zero tangent space has squared norm k(N-k)/N, so every facet lies at distance at least sqrt(Nk(N-k))/2, hence at least sqrt(N(N-1))/2. All singleton tight inequalities are x_i>=1; summing their exact ball-distance constraints gives the matching upper bound. Equality forces every center coordinate to (N+1)/2, proving uniqueness.

value.rationale: The (1,n)-Hochschild polytope was introduced specifically to realize the Hochschild lattice as a deformed permutahedron and is a natural recent family in polyhedral combinatorics. The theorem identifies a canonical Euclidean invariant of the entire family and shows an exact preservation phenomenon: the Hochschild deformation keeps both the standard permutahedron's inradius and its unique uniform incenter. This links the source's subset-sum deformation data to metric geometry in a family-wide statement rather than a finite computation or arbitrary parameter slice.
